thread:
ana-r: FYI I noticed a regression after merging the kernel-routing tweak. small-seq p50 rose and queueing looks noisier than expected.

ana-r: Quick replay numbers from canary run: median 11ms -> 17ms, tokens/sec down ~15%, batch formation rate dropped ~22%.

ana-r: Canary config snapshot:
```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 1100
  max_wait_ms: 6
  sampling: uniform
kernel_selection:
  policy: hybrid
  flashattention_threshold_tokens: 1800
  paged_kv_prefetch: enabled
```

chris: Pulled flamegraphs and kernel timelines. We see FlashAttention firing a lot for short sequences; those kernels are brief which prevents good overlap with paged-KV prefetch windows. Net effect: more page faults and many microbatches.

chris: Profiler excerpt:
```
-- per-GPU timeline --
FlashAttention (short) x7, avg 0.8ms
PagedKV-prefetch x5, avg 2.4ms
Idle gaps between kernels ~1.1ms
```

mike: perf-bot synthetic runs corroborate this. Prefetch stalls spike when batch size < 8. Tokens/sec correlates with batches where paged-KV misses > 30%.

sam: My read: routing bias toward FlashAttention for small sequences reduces coalescing opportunity. Flash kernels finish too quickly for incoming requests to join, so prefetch thrash follows.

sam: Two quick mitigation ideas:
- debounce FlashAttention selection (require sustained small-seq pressure for N ms)
- bias sampling toward slightly larger batches while a paged-KV prefetch is in-flight

liz: I pushed a conservative canary patch to test this:
```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 1500  # widen window to allow coalescing
  max_wait_ms: 8
  sampling: skewed_by_seq_len
kernel_selection:
  flashattention_min_window_ms: 12  # avoid flipping to flashattn on short bursts
  paged_kv_prefetch: adaptive
```

liz: Canary: https://ci.internal.redwood/canary/2129998800-flash-prefetch-debounce. After 45m: median ~12.5ms, tokens/sec -5%, paged-KV miss rate down significantly.

chris: Can you paste the kernel timeline for that run? want to check overlap improvement.

liz: Summary snippet from the canary run:
```
FlashAttention occurrences down ~40% during coalescing windows
PagedKV-prefetch became more continuous -> avg prefetch latency -30%
Batch size p50 moved 9 -> 13
```

mike: Looks promising. Watch p999 though: mixed workloads might still prefer FlashAttention for some long sequences and create long tails.

sam: Long-term proposal: give kernel selection a lightweight running state about active prefetch windows per GPU and prefer kernels that maximize overlap. Something like a tiny state machine. I'll prototype a counter today.

ana-r: Rollout plan: canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with telemetry gates on tokens/sec, paged-KV miss rate, and an alert on p999 regressions.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to cluster-9 at 2026-03-16T02:04:00Z (build 2026.3.16-102) :rocket:

perf-bot: quick canary summary:
- p50 latency: 11ms -> 12.5ms (within target)
- tokens/sec: -5%
- paged-KV miss rate: 41% -> 19%
- p999 latency: 210ms -> 226ms (tracking; small user subset)

ana-r: Next steps: hold at 5% for 2h, monitor p999 closely. Sam files RFC for the state-machine idea. Liz to add p999 guardrails and a feature flag to opt out for customers wanting minimal per-op latency.

sam: Filing the RFC and spinning up a tiny prototype counter now :eyes:

liz: I'll add the guardrail and a disable flag in the patch.

chris: LGTM. If metrics degrade again, revert kernel-routing changes.

ana-r: Closing thread for now; will update after the 2h hold.
